//: Mutation matrix for CROSS-SOURCE MUSIC IDENTITY (issue #194), driven by probe_musicid. Every mutant is labelled with the DIRECTION it breaks in, because that is the whole point of this list: a matcher biased to refuse passes every over-merge test by doing nothing, so a suite with only over-merge mutants proves nothing. Half of these make it merge too eagerly (a wrong merge HIDES music); half stop it merging at all (which is the failure a lazy probe cannot see).

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-edition-strip-needs-no-strong-word
mutants.//: The strong-noise requirement is the whole safety property of the edition strip. Without it '(Live)', '(Mono)', '(Demo)' and a bare '(2009)' are all droppable runs of weak tokens, and a live album merges into the studio album it is named after.
mutants.find: return strong;

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-year-gate-removed
mutants.//: The year is the only evidence that separates two records whose titles are identical. Drop it and a 1983 live album fuses with the 1980 studio album.
mutants.find:
if (a.year > 0 && b.year > 0 && std::abs(a.year - b.year) > 1)
        return Confidence::TooLowToMerge;

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-roman-value-cap-removed
mutants.//: MIX is a valid Roman numeral (1009), and so are CD, DC, MC, MI and XL. The 1..30 bound is what keeps ordinary English words out of the levelling; without it 'Discovery Mix' normalises to 'discovery 1009'.
mutants.find: if (v <= 0 || v > kMaxLevelledRoman) continue;

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-single-token-title-is-levelled
mutants.//: Starting the levelling loop at 0 levels a title that is NOTHING but a numeral, so the album called 'II' becomes the album called '2'.

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-a-disagreeing-MBID-stops-refusing
mutants.//: Ground truth has to cut BOTH ways. If a different release id only falls silent instead of refusing, two records MusicBrainz says are different merge on their titles.
mutants.find: if (!ar.isEmpty() && !br.isEmpty()) return ar == br ? Ground::Same : Ground::Different;
mutants.replace: if (!ar.isEmpty() && !br.isEmpty()) return ar == br ? Ground::Same : Ground::Silent;

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-albums-ignore-the-artist
mutants.//: Without the artist gate every self-titled record in the library is one record, and 'Weezer' by Weezer merges with 'Weezer' by anybody else.
mutants.find:
if (!sameArtist(a.albumArtist, a.artistMbid, b.albumArtist, b.artistMbid))
        return Confidence::TooLowToMerge;

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-the-untagged-buckets-of-two-sources-fuse
mutants.//: The largest wrong merge available: two sources' unnameable artists are two different piles of files, and matching them makes one of the piles unreachable.
mutants.find: if (na.isEmpty() || nb.isEmpty()) return Confidence::TooLowToMerge;

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-a-negative-override-is-ignored
mutants.//: 'These are not the same album' is the one row that can give a hidden record back. If the store's 0 verdict stops refusing, the button appears to do nothing.
mutants.replace:
const int said = verdictForKeys(kAlbumGroup, ka, kb);
    if (said == 1) return Confidence::Certain;

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-two-copies-from-one-source-merge
mutants.//: A supplier has already grouped its own library; fusing two rows it kept apart hides one of them, and does it to a source that was perfectly correct. The guard is on the UNION, so this also covers the transitive route.
mutants.find:
for (const QString& s : std::as_const(sources_[rb]))
            if (sources_[ra].contains(s)) return false;

mutants.name: TOO-EAGER-every-token-joins-the-acronym-run
mutants.//: The run predicate is what makes the acronym rule safe: only SINGLE-character tokens join one. Widen it and 'Kid A' becomes 'kida' and 'OK Computer' becomes 'okcomputer', fusing titles that differ by a real word. (The >= 2 threshold below it is deliberately NOT mutated: joining a one-token run yields that token, so it is the same answer as >= 1 and no mutation of it can change behaviour.)
mutants.find: while (j < toks.size() && toks.at(j).size() == 1) ++j;

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-acronyms-are-not-collapsed
mutants.//: The other end of it. 'U.S.A.' arrives as three tokens and 'USA' as one, and 'R.E.M.' / 'REM' is the same problem in an artist name - a spelling difference two suppliers disagree about constantly.
mutants.find:
toks = collapseAcronyms(toks);
    for (QString& t : toks) t = canonicalSequelWord(t);

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-only-certain-counts
mutants.//: THE DIRECTION A LAZY PROBE CANNOT SEE. Narrow merges() to Certain and the string matcher stops mattering at all: nothing without an MBID or a user verdict ever merges, and the whole feature quietly becomes a no-op that passes every over-merge test.
mutants.find: inline bool merges(Confidence c) { return c == Confidence::Certain || c == Confidence::Likely; }
mutants.replace: inline bool merges(Confidence c) { return c == Confidence::Certain; }

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-year-must-match-exactly
mutants.//: One year of slack absorbs the ordinary release-date drift between a rip and a server's own metadata. Tighten it and half of a real library stops merging.
mutants.find: std::abs(a.year - b.year) > 1)

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-track-count-becomes-a-gate
mutants.//: The issue says track count is a TIEBREAK. Promote it to a gate and the commonest real case - one source has the bonus disc - stops merging, which is a duplicate for every deluxe edition anybody owns.

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-edition-noise-is-never-stripped
mutants.//: The other end of the first mutant. Strip nothing and 'OK Computer' never matches 'OK Computer [2009 Remaster]', which is the single commonest way one album is spelled twice.
mutants.find:
if (toks.isEmpty()) return false;
    bool strong = false;
mutants.replace:
if (true) return false;
    bool strong = false;

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-roman-numerals-are-not-levelled
mutants.//: 'Pt. II' and 'Part 2' are the same record. Levelling on BOTH sides is what the romhack matcher in this repo needed and did not have.
mutants.find:
if (afterSequelWord || trailingNumeral)
            toks[i] = QString::number(v);

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-volume-is-not-vol
mutants.//: 'Vol.', 'Vol' and 'Volume' are one word written three ways, and a library and a server will disagree about which one inside the same album's tags.
mutants.find: if (t == QLatin1String("volume")) return QStringLiteral("vol");

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-an-agreeing-MBID-falls-silent
mutants.//: Ground truth is supposed to beat the heuristic in the POSITIVE direction too: a reissue whose year is decades off its original still shares a release id, and that is the whole reason MBIDs are worth reading.

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-featured-artist-noise-is-kept
mutants.//: 'Jay-Z feat. Alicia Keys' is Jay-Z. Keep the tail and every guest credit founds an artist of its own on one source and not the other.
mutants.find:
toks = toks.mid(0, i);
            break;

mutants.name: SINGLE-SOURCE-GUARANTEE-short-circuit-removed
mutants.//: Not a matching mutant at all - a compatibility one. With one supplier the index must come back out untouched and `active` must stay false, because that is what makes 'a user with only a local library sees exactly what they see today' a structural claim rather than a hope.
mutants.find: if (live.size() == 1) { out.idx = *live.first()->index; return out; }

mutants.name: STOPS-MERGING-merged-artist-trackcount-is-the-primary-instance
mutants.//: The #194 increment 1 rule, restored: a merged artist reports the PRIMARY instance's track count. A remote primary reports 0, which withheld 'Play all' and 'Shuffle all' from every server-backed artist - the two verbs that are the only multi-album queues this app can build, and with them crossfade and ReplayGain's track mode. It also understates a local primary, whose merged discography includes the server-only records beside it.
